approach: Centralize authority in host/state, normalize authoritative Driver observations, exhaustively route Codex app-server messages, replace the legacy wire in one flag-day cutover, and render one checked-in semantic matrix.

out_of_scope: Raw agent events on client wire

units.title: Implement composite status reducer and signal identity
units.objective: Make valid facets, pending IDs, precedence, and epoch/sequence the host-state authority.
units.output_format: Go production code plus reducer/view tests.
units.tool_guidance: Use typed operations and pure reducer tests; preserve accepted spinner/text accessibility contracts.
units.task_boundaries: Do not implement Driver routing or client rendering.
acceptance: Spinner and ! are exclusive; bell and ! can coexist.
Invalid internal states fail fast.

units.title: Implement Codex exhaustive router and held-request lifecycle
units.objective: Classify known methods, bound unknown diagnostics, and terminalize held requests once.
units.output_format: Go router code, fake, contract tests, and FakeVsReal backstop.
units.tool_guidance: Use an explicit inventory and atomic map removal linearization point.
units.task_boundaries: Do not alter common presentation mapping.
acceptance: Known methods have exactly one disposition.
Late/duplicate resolution cannot double reply or leave stale !.

units.title: Implement all-driver normalizers and remove Codex OSC inference
units.objective: Give every Driver an authoritative source table and common typed operation output.
units.output_format: Driver/runtime adapters and table-driven/Harness regression tests.
units.tool_guidance: Retain Shell OSC 133; delete only OSC 0/2/notification status authority.
units.task_boundaries: Do not introduce a new Shell protocol.
acceptance: Codex, Claude, Gemini, Grok, and Shell cover supported/unsupported/malformed/unavailable.
Codex OSC 0/2 and BEL cannot mutate facets; Claude/Gemini and Shell retain their existing OSC contracts.

units.title: Replace the wire schema and regenerate every SDK atomically
units.objective: Delete the legacy scalar status and all fallback producers while landing the composite-only server, generated SDKs, and all clients in one revision.
units.output_format: Composite-only schema/server projection, regenerated SDKs, migrated Web/Workspace/Windows Shell clients, and zero-legacy contract fixtures.
units.tool_guidance: Regenerate every SDK from the canonical schema and make generation cleanliness, repository zero-legacy searches, gateway fixtures, and all-client builds one cutover gate.
units.task_boundaries: Do not add mixed-version support, scalar projection, legacy event fallback, OSC status inference, or runtime rollback mode.
acceptance: The server, all generated SDKs, Web, Workspace, and Windows Shell use only the composite shape in the same revision.
The legacy scalar field, legacy event fallback, and OSC status inference have zero producers and consumers.
Any stale SDK or partial client migration fails the atomic cutover gate.

units.output_format: Checked-in fixture, renderer changes, DOM/accessibility/UIA tests.

units.task_boundaries: Do not put glyph metadata on the runtime wire.
acceptance: All semantic keys and accessible labels match.
Unknown is dedicated; spinner+! is impossible; bell+! passes.

requirements.ears: The system shall keep a driver-neutral composite session status as the sole status authority and shall not delegate status decisions to clients or terminal titles.
acceptance: The same typed operations produce the same snapshot for every Driver.
An OSC title cannot mutate the snapshot.

requirements.ears: When a Codex app-server message is received, the router shall classify every known notification, server request, response, lifecycle, elicitation, and tool-proposal method into exactly one stateful or explicit no-state-effect disposition.
acceptance: The checked-in inventory has no unclassified known method.
Unknown methods use the diagnostic path.

requirements.ears: When an unknown, malformed, or inventory-unavailable structured message is observed, the system shall preserve the current trustworthy facets and emit a bounded correlated diagnostic without fabricating idle or another status.
requirements.rationale: Preserves forward compatibility without false state.
acceptance: Unknown and malformed are distinguishable.
Diagnostic floods are rate-limited and bounded.

requirements.ears: While at least one unresolved human-input request exists, the system shall expose human input required, suppress the activity spinner, and terminalize each request exactly once on resolution, cancellation, expiry, or connection loss.
requirements.rationale: Fixes spinner/! exclusivity and request lifecycle.
acceptance: Spinner and ! never coexist.
One remaining request keeps ! visible.

requirements.ears: When a notification-worthy event occurs, the system shall issue a transient monotonically identified signal that may coexist with human input required and shall not replace the base status.
requirements.rationale: Bell is a signal, not state.
acceptance: Bell and ! may coexist.
A client does not replay an already consumed signal in the same server epoch.

requirements.ears: The system shall normalize Codex, Claude, Gemini, Grok, and Shell authoritative observations through one typed facet-operation contract and shall produce explicit unsupported, malformed, or unavailable outcomes instead of title-based inference.
requirements.rationale: Applies the common contract to all Drivers.
acceptance: Every Driver has an authoritative-source row and exhaustive disposition.
Codex Driver does not read OSC 0/2 as agent status; other Drivers retain their existing observation contracts.

requirements.ears: Web, Workspace, and Windows Shell shall consume only the composite session-status wire and render the same semantic visual key, animation rule, and accessible label from the shared matrix without Driver branching, legacy scalar status, legacy event fallback, or OSC-derived status.
acceptance: Parity fixtures pass in all three clients against the regenerated composite-only SDKs.
Unknown has a dedicated visual and label; stale last-known and every legacy status fallback are absent.
Repository search and schema fixtures prove that the legacy scalar status is no longer emitted or consumed.

requirements.ears: If OSC 0/2 title, BEL, or OSC notification is received without an authoritative structured observation, the system shall not change agent session facets, while Shell OSC 133 prompt semantics shall remain operational.
requirements.rationale: Removes agent OSC inference without breaking shell prompts.
acceptance: Conflicting OSC cannot override structured status.
OSC 133 regression tests pass.

requirements.ears: When failure or connection loss occurs, the system shall expose a failure indication distinct from human input required and shall drain held requests with correlated diagnostics.
acceptance: Failure never renders as !.
Connection loss drains pending requests exactly once.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: The composite status wire shall replace the legacy scalar status as an intentional breaking flag-day change: server schema, generated SDKs, Web, Workspace, and Windows Shell shall land atomically, with no mixed-version support, compatibility projection, legacy event fallback, or OSC status inference.
non_functional_requirements.verification: Composite-only schema fixtures, regenerated-SDK cleanliness, repository-wide zero-legacy searches, all-client compile/tests, and gateway contract tests must pass in the same revision.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Status shall not depend on color or motion alone and all clients shall publish the same accessible name.
non_functional_requirements.verification: DOM, accessibility tree, and UIA assertions consume the shared matrix.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Protocol and display inventory additions shall fail an invariant-naming contract test when unclassified.
non_functional_requirements.verification: Fake, FakeVsReal, and contract tests form the external-dependency triple.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Unknown diagnostics and transient signals shall use bounded memory and non-blocking backpressure.
non_functional_requirements.verification: Flood and sequence-bound tests prove fixed caps and explicit drops.

acceptance.criterion: User-reachable snapshots prove spinner+! impossible and bell+! possible.
Every Driver has an exhaustive source row and OSC status input changes no facets.
Web DOM, Workspace accessibility, and Windows UIA publish the same matrix labels.

adrs.title: Use a valid composite status model with presentation precedence
adrs.context: Activity, unresolved human input, failure, and signal have different lifecycles; a scalar loses observable combinations.
adrs.decision: Own tagged lifecycle/failure and pending-request IDs in host/state. Derive ! from a non-empty pending set, choose ! over spinner, keep failure distinct, and treat signal as orthogonal.
consequences: Spinner and ! are structurally exclusive.
Bell and ! may coexist.
Invalid internal combinations fail fast.

alternatives.why_not: Cannot preserve concurrent signal and human-input semantics.

status_provenance.rationale: Codex TUIで裏取りした複合状態モデルで進める指示。

adrs.title: Identify transient signals by server epoch and monotonic sequence
adrs.context: Snapshot replay must neither duplicate a signal on reconnect nor suppress new signals after restart.
adrs.decision: The status owner issues (serverEpoch, signalSequence). Each client keeps an in-process highest-consumed marker per session/epoch; reconnect does not replay, and client or server restart resets the consumption scope.
consequences: Reconnect behavior is deterministic.
No durable user configuration is introduced.
A client restart may replay the latest still-present signal once; the signal is non-authoritative and transient.

alternatives.why_not: Adds persistence and cross-device semantics outside scope.

status_provenance.rationale: bellを状態ではなく一過性signalとして扱う方針の承認。

adrs.title: Use a build-time Codex method inventory with runtime unknown diagnostics
adrs.context: The real app-server does not provide a dependable connection-time protocol-version handshake for routing authority.
adrs.decision: Bind a checked-in inventory to the supported Codex version and route every known method explicitly. Use fake, FakeVsReal, and invariant-naming contract tests; unknown and malformed messages preserve state and enter bounded diagnostics.
consequences: Protocol drift is visible and testable.
Runtime does not depend on a nonexistent handshake.
Inventory updates accompany Codex upgrades.

alternatives.why_not: No verified authoritative runtime source exists.

status_provenance.rationale: app-server eventを正確に全てhandleする要求の実装方針。

adrs.title: Normalize authoritative Driver events and keep Shell limited-capability
adrs.context: Drivers expose different evidence; inventing a new Shell protocol or retaining title inference would split authority.
adrs.decision: Codex uses app-server; Claude/Gemini/Grok use structured driver/runtime lifecycle sources; Shell uses process lifecycle and retained OSC 133 prompt boundaries only. Codex OSC 0/2 and notification/BEL status inference is removed; Claude/Gemini and Shell retain their existing OSC observation contracts.
consequences: All Drivers implement one operation contract.
Shell reports unsupported detail as unknown.
OSC 133 remains intact.

status_provenance.rationale: OSC状態推定を削除し全Driverを共通契約へ正規化する要求。

adrs.title: Migrate composite status with a temporary deterministic scalar projection
adrs.context: Three clients and generated SDKs cannot switch atomically.
adrs.decision: Add composite fields server-first while retaining a deterministic scalar projection; update generated SDKs and all clients; remove legacy status only after a zero-consumer and baseline/target fixture gate.
consequences: Mixed versions remain parseable.
Legacy semantics are explicit, not client-invented.
Removal requires evidence.

status_provenance.rationale: 旧scalar status、旧event、OSC推定への互換projectionやfallbackを明示的に不要とした。

adrs.title: Use one checked-in language-neutral status display matrix
adrs.context: API metadata and independent client mappings create competing owners and runtime payload complexity.
adrs.decision: Keep one checked-in semantic-key fixture consumed directly by parity tests and renderer adapters. Do not place glyph metadata on the runtime wire. Use dedicated unknown rather than stale last-known.
consequences: All clients share labels and allowed combinations.
Unknown cannot masquerade as current state.
Native renderers remain free to use platform glyph implementations within the fixed semantic role.

alternatives.why_not: Couples presentation assets to runtime wire and duplicates native mapping boundaries.
Can present unauthoritative state as current.

status_provenance.rationale: Windows Shell、Workspace、Web UIの表示統一要求。

adrs.title: Replace the legacy scalar status wire in one atomic flag-day cutover
adrs.context: The user explicitly rejects backward compatibility and fallback. Keeping a scalar projection, legacy event fallback, or OSC status inference would preserve multiple authorities and allow clients to observe divergent status semantics.
adrs.decision: Replace the legacy scalar status with the composite status wire as a breaking flag-day change. In the same landed change, remove the legacy scalar field, legacy event fallback, and OSC 0/2, BEL, and OSC notification status inference; regenerate every SDK and update Web, Workspace, and Windows Shell atomically. No mixed-version operation or runtime rollback fallback is supported.
consequences: Every in-repository consumer moves to the composite contract in one commit.
Old clients and SDKs are intentionally incompatible with the new server wire.
Repository-wide generation, compile, contract, and client parity gates prevent a partial cutover.

alternatives.option: Temporary scalar projection and mixed-version rollout
alternatives.why_not: Rejected by explicit user consultation because it retains legacy authority and fallback behavior.

alternatives.option: Composite wire with legacy event or OSC inference fallback
alternatives.why_not: Would split status authority and permit old observations to repopulate the replacement model.

status_provenance.rationale: The user explicitly selected a flag-day composite replacement with no backward compatibility or fallback.

observable_effects.description: A language-neutral checked-in fixture is the sole semantic matrix; status-wire supplies semantic keys but does not carry glyph metadata; Web, Workspace, and Windows Shell render and test the same key, animation, glyph role, and accessible label. Active uses spinner, unresolved input uses !, failure uses a distinct glyph, and unknown uses a dedicated unknown visual. Adversarially: The matrix cannot encode spinner+!; bell+! is allowed; unknown never displays last-known as current; fixture/schema changes land before renderer updates and parity gates reject missing or extra keys. Existing visible text, shape/color/label redundancy, and functional spinner behavior from accepted ADRs remain.
